ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human safety review with the chat log attached; no fare or fee adjustment to the $32.86 RydeX fare; no account action from this file (F7, F8 show no prior upheld disputes), and confirm with the rider that 995 / commercial-insurance / RydeHELP reporting paths are open if she wishes to pursue a safety complaint.
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety dispute with a system-flagged threat message in the chat record: rider requested to get out at 17:19 [F3], driver replied at 17:20 "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], keyword-tagged as a threat [F5]. Driver's statement offers a safety justification (rider tried to open the door while moving) [F6]; no GPS or telematics fact records the doors or whether the car stopped between 17:19 and drop-off. Profile facts show no prior pattern on either side [F7][F8]. Human review needed to weigh the threat wording against the driver's account.

rejected_claims.reason: Rejected as a basis for a non-safety disposition: the keyword tag F5 is indeed derived from the same message F4, but the escalation trigger under SAFE-1 is the verbatim driver chat content itself [F4][F5][SAFE-1]; the driver advocate separately conceded this point (D5 of the rebuttal), and the trace records the threat-language element as settled.

Accurate but immaterial: F1 shows no excess distance over the 15.5 km optimal route and the RydeX fare of $32.86 was a fixed quote, so no fare refund arises [F1][FARE-1]; this does not answer the safety escalation the rider actually requested.

Partially rejected: F7 and F8 do show zero disputes and zero upheld disputes, so no RD-6 account flag applies here [F7][F8][RD-6], but that absence of a prior pattern cannot be used to close a live threat-in-chat safety complaint, which SAFE-1 routes to human review [F4][F5][SAFE-1].

Withdrawn/not relied on: F5 is only a keyword tag of the words already in F4, so it adds no independent corroboration [F4][F5][SAFE-1]; the escalation stands on F4 itself and no separate weight is given to F5.

Not sustained as a finding: F6 is the driver's own statement and, under the procedural rule that system records outweigh statements, it cannot establish either the threat or the justification; it is preserved only as the driver's competing account for the human reviewer [F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1].
